title: Rochdale covered as GMP marks 1,825 domestic abuse protection orders
excerpt: Domestic Abuse Protection Orders are now used in every Greater Manchester Police district, including Rochdale. The force says 1,825 have been issued across Greater Manchester since the pilot began.
body:
Domestic Abuse Protection Orders are now in use across every Greater Manchester Police district, including Rochdale, as the force marks two years since the scheme began.

GMP says 1,825 orders have been issued across Greater Manchester since the pilot started in Bury in November 2024. The force completed its rollout to all 12 districts in March 2026.

The 1,825 figure is force-wide. GMP has not supplied a separate total for Rochdale, nor a district-by-district breakdown.

The orders, known as DAPOs, can protect people from physical, sexual and financial abuse, as well as controlling or coercive behaviour. They are not limited to current or former partners and can apply where the person causing harm is a family member or another person known to the victim.

Courts can tailor an order to the risks in an individual case. Conditions can prohibit contact in person or online, require someone to stay away from a home, or place positive requirements on the person subject to the order. Breaching an order is a criminal offence and can lead to arrest.

GMP says officers can seek an order without requiring a victim to make the application themselves. The force said this can reduce the burden on survivors when officers identify a risk that requires protection.

The force has recorded more than 700 breaches since the pilot began. That is also a Greater Manchester total, and no separate Rochdale figure was provided.

Assistant Chief Constable Steph Parker, GMP's lead for vulnerability, said the orders had strengthened the force's response to domestic abuse. She added: "Nobody should have to face this, and definitely not alone."

Kate Green, Deputy Mayor of Greater Manchester, said: "Our message is very simple: DAPOs work." She said resources now needed to match the ambition behind the legislation.

The Greater Manchester milestone comes as DAPOs are rolled out across England and Wales from 25 November 2026. The Home Office and Ministry of Justice say the orders bring together protections previously available through several routes and can remain in place for as long as a court considers necessary.

For Rochdale residents, the key point is that these protections are available through the local GMP district as well as through the courts. Anyone in immediate danger should call 999. Non-emergency reports can be made by calling 101 or through GMP's website and Live Chat service.

People can seek support without making a police report. The Greater Manchester Domestic Abuse Helpline provides advice from 10am to 4pm, Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays, at https://www.domesticabusehelpline.co.uk/. Local services can also be found through End the Fear at https://www.endthefear.co.uk/help-if-you-are-being-hurt/getting-help-in-your-area/.

Source: Greater Manchester Police press release issued on 25 November 2026; Home Office and Ministry of Justice guidance published on 24 and 25 November 2026.
